correctness.rationale: A fresh enumeration from the two stated host graphs grouped the eight-edge perfect matchings by their six-edge subsets. Distinct matchings sharing six edges differ in exactly two different pairings of the same four vertices, hence in precisely one alternating four-cycle. All-source BFS on this alternative construction verified R: 2016 states, 6048 switches, component sizes 1368, 288 twice, and 72 isolated; S: 1920 states, 5280 switches, component size 1908 and 12 isolated. The radii/diameters (7,8), (14,14), (10,13), and all 576 degree-three vertices in the two 288 components were reproduced. The direct rook isolation proof also checks: exactly one horizontal edge per row and one vertical per column are necessary, horizontal pairs form an assigned C4 on the columns, and complementary incident-row pairs give distinct vertical pairs. Mixed pairs cannot switch: if the horizontal row meets the vertical edge, the needed same-column horizontal vertex would coincide with its endpoint; otherwise both horizontal vertices would need the vertical column.
residual_risks: The frozen JSON checker tests the stated strong regularity parameters of the host data rather than binding each edge to the two definitions by itself; the fresh run starts with the explicit coordinate formulas, as do the original generators. No inference is made for longer switches.

value.rationale: Rook and Shrikhande are the canonical same-parameter nonisomorphic pair. Their complete switch profiles give a concrete witness that those parameters do not control the frozen states or the exact distances in this natural reconfiguration process. The two cubic diameter-14 rook components and the single large Shrikhande component are more informative than simply observing that both switch chains are disconnected.
residual_risks: Neither mixing times nor behavior of other strongly regular graphs is determined.
